agent_judgment.rationale: 28M, nonsmoker, with left-sided pleuritic chest pain starting the day after a heavy chest workout. He denies shortness of breath and leg swelling. Musculoskeletal strain (pectoral or intercostal) is most likely. However, new pleuritic chest pain in a young man also raises small spontaneous pneumothorax (heavy lifting can trigger it, and pleuritic pain may be the only symptom), pericarditis, and, much less likely, PE or pneumonia. With no dyspnea, PE risk is low, though heart rate and SpO2 are unknown for full PERC. Nothing reported requires emergency care. A physician should confirm musculoskeletal features (reproducible tenderness, pain with arm or torso movement, gradual onset) and screen for red flags before attributing this to a strain. Ibuprofen is reasonable if he has no contraindications. Clear musculoskeletal features keep this async with home care. Absent musculoskeletal features moves it to an in-person exam within 48h, likely with ECG and chest X-ray. Any red flag moves it to emergency care now.
